items.claim: A Windows service whose binary directory is writable by the current principal lets a tester drop a replacement executable into that directory and have the service start it after a stop/start cycle.
items.body:
A Windows service whose binary directory is writable by the current principal lets a tester drop a replacement executable into that directory and have the service start it after a stop/start cycle.

HackTricks reference: 151098c3 (notion:151098c3-95c5-8060-be35-c392789893fc)
items.disproof: The directory ACL denies write to the current principal, or the service keeps loading a binary at a path other than the uploaded one, so the uploaded file never runs.

items.claim: When the service binary cannot be overwritten in place but the service configuration can be changed, repointing the service's binPath at an uploaded executable makes the service host the attacker's file instead.
items.body:
When the service binary cannot be overwritten in place but the service configuration can be changed, repointing the service's binPath at an uploaded executable makes the service host the attacker's file instead.

HackTricks reference: 151098c3 (notion:151098c3-95c5-8060-be35-c392789893fc)
items.disproof: The binPath change is rejected or the query still reports the original executable, so the uploaded file is never loaded by the service.
